title: Model-drift escalation bridge and customer remediation pathways
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Multiple recent canary rollouts surfaced divergent model behavior: one hosted canary produced hallucinations on a finance-related prompt set, a Dedicated cluster saw latency-induced token truncation under burst load, and a Private deployment reported inconsistent structured output formatting after a quantized model variant rollout. These incidents triggered customer escalations with different SLAs and ownership models. Goal: Create and validate an operational playbook and automation to coordinate escalations and rapid remediation across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private environments when model rollouts cause regressions or canary failures. This ticket covers the escalation bridge (single coordination path), automated mitigations (circuit breaker + pinning), customer communication templates, and validation tests for the rollback automation across deployment modes.
acceptance_criteria: An escalation bridge flow documented with primary/secondary contacts and decision gates for Hosted/Dedicated/Private incidents.

Automated circuit-breaker that can pause rollouts and route traffic to pinned stable model variants for all three deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) with documented API calls and a test harness.
A verified rollback runbook that preserves customer data sovereignty constraints for Private deployments and includes a checklist for Dedicated capacity controllers.
Customer communication templates for P0 regressions that include impact, mitigation steps, ETA, and rollback confirmation.
Integration test suite that simulates three failure classes (semantic regression, latency truncation, structured output drift) and validates the end-to-end rollback path in staging environments.
Post-deployment audit entries appear in Console audit logs and provide traceability from canary decision to rollback completion.
runbook_steps: 1) Triage and immediate bridge: On detection (alert or customer escal), oncall creates dedicated Zoom bridge and tags SMEs: runtime, model-ops, infra, and account team.

2) Quick mitigation: Enable circuit-breaker API -> set rollout_state=paused across the target region/cluster; if hosted, route new requests to stable-pinned model; for Dedicated, switch target pool config to pinned-gpu-pool; for Private, instruct customer operator shortcut (documented API call + CLI).
3) Impact assessment: Run canonical prompt set (canary suite) against pinned and candidate models to confirm regression outlines (semantic vs structural vs perf). Attach fails to incident ticket.

4) Decide: If regression is high-impact (customer-facing or security-sensitive) perform immediate rollback; for medium impact perform canary shrink and additional validation; low impact schedule fix in next minor rollout.

5) Execute rollback: Use rollout-control service to create rollback plan, set pinned version, and trigger gradual traffic switch with observability checks (latency, tokenization errors, structured-output validation).

6) Customer comms: Send initial acknowledgement within 30 minutes (template available), send mitigation update at 2 hours with ETA, confirm rollback completion and follow-up with RCA timeline within 72 hours.
7) Post-incident: Run regression hunting and add failing prompts to continuous evals, update model catalog with compatibility notes, and schedule a dedicated follow-up with affected customers.
